summary.intent: Finalize a feature branch (full Rust test suite, build/typecheck, push, draft PR) then run the /simplify cleanup pass over the PR diff to improve code quality before merge.
summary.outcome: Draft PR opened; 4 parallel review agents (reuse, simplification, efficiency, altitude) audited the diff, fixes were applied via 2 domain-split agents (Rust, wasm/client), all gates (Rust workspace fmt/clippy/test, client vitest/typecheck/build, browser conformance suite with fresh wasm build) passed on the combined tree, and the simplify fixes were committed.

repo: CipherBox has a multi-language gate sequence for changes touching both Rust and TS: Rust workspace (fmt/clippy/test) + client (vitest/typecheck/build) + a separate browser conformance suite that requires a fresh wasm build — all three must be re-run after any cross-cutting fix.

packages/client and crates/wasm are tightly coupled (host.rs, broadcast/transport files, worker/serve.ts, browser test harness) — changes in this session touched both sides together, consistent with the wasm boundary being a frequent cross-cutting surface.
workflow: /simplify skill pattern: 4 independent review agents in parallel (reuse, simplification, efficiency, altitude angles) against the diff, then dedup and apply fixes via separate agents split by domain (here: Rust crates vs. wasm/client packages) rather than one monolithic apply pass.
After applying simplify fixes across a large multi-language diff, re-run the full gate suite (not just the touched packages) before committing, since fixes can span crate/package boundaries.
